info.title: API: Mapping
info.description: Hotel and room mapping APIs. Map partner hotel IDs to LiteAPI catalogue hotels, and map or group supplier room names against your room catalog. Room matching: **Implementation Workflow** (`implementation-workflow`).

partner.description: Partner name. Pass this exact string as the `partner` form field when mapping IDs (matching is case-insensitive upstream).

mappings.description: Number of known ID mappings for this partner — a proxy for inventory coverage size.

MappingSummary.description: Outcome counts returned in the `X-Mapping-Summary` response header after a partner ID mapping run.

matched.description: Rows successfully mapped to Nuitee inventory

review.description: Rows that need manual review (ambiguous candidates)

not_found.description: Partner IDs with no match in Nuitee inventory

invalid.description: Rows that could not be parsed or validated

input_gcs.description: GCS URI of the input CSV

output_gcs.description: Optional GCS URI for the result CSV

i.description: Supplier row index (stable within the request)

predictedLabel.description: 1 if the candidate is a positive match at the decision threshold, otherwise 0

selected.description: Best match when status is mapped; null otherwise

name.description: Mapped reference room name, or not_mapped when rejected

id.description: Mapped reference room id, or 0 when not mapped

reason.description: Short human explanation when not mapped
reason.example: Run-of-house rate; no specific room type

p.description: Source supplier of the supplier room name: the job `provider`, the room's `supplierRooms[].provider`, merged with the provider already stored on the mapping. A sorted, `|`-joined set when several providers sent the room. Absent for direct suppliers and when no provider was supplied.

previous.description: Prior cache mapping for this room, if any

reason.description: Short human explanation when not mapped

source.description: How the final decision was produced: our internal audit LLM (internal_llm), the audit omitted the room (internal_llm_omitted), an advisory adjustment to an existing mapping (internal_llm_adjustment), the deterministic attribute guard rejecting an audit verdict (attribute_guard), or the guest-promise score rejecting an audit verdict on a hard stop or a score below 0.60 (promise_score).

crossEncoder.description: Legacy cross-encoder proposal. Always null: deep-map audits against the full catalog without cross-encoder pre-scoring. Use score instead.

type.description: Normalised bed type. Labels are canonicalised: 'Extra-large double bed (Super-king size)' becomes extra_large_double, 'Queen bed' becomes queen.

label.description: Bed description as stated by the source.

count.description: Number of beds of this type.

RoomAttributes.description: Optional structured evidence about a room. Omitted fields mean the source did not state them, never that the room lacks them. Values are free-form: known variants are canonicalised (structure synonyms, both/either, m2/m²/sqft), the rest are lower-cased and trimmed and kept rather than rejected. Only unusable input is refused: negative counts, a non-positive size, a size without a unit, empty bed types and duplicate feature keys. At most 4 KiB per room's attributes and 256 KiB across a list.

structure.description: Room structure as stated by the source. Free-form: known variants are canonicalised (bungalow, chalet and cottage become villa; condo becomes apartment), anything else is kept lower-cased and trimmed. Do not infer it from a marketing room name.

tier.description: Commercial tier stated by the source (standard, premium, deluxe, ...).

bedrooms.description: Stated bedroom count for multi-room structures. 0 or omitted means not stated.

bedRelation.description: How the listed beds relate. Free-form: both and all become and, either and alternatives become or; anything else is kept lower-cased and trimmed.

size.description: Stated floor area, normalised to square metres.

unit.description: Square metres by convention. m2, m² and sqft are converted to sqm; any other unit is kept as stated.

views.description: Normalised view labels. 'City View' and 'city' converge on city.

accessibility.description: Normalised accessibility features stated by the source (for example mobility_accessible, roll_in_shower). Never inferred from a room name.

features.description: Only attributes the source stated as true or false; a missing key means unknown, not false. Informational, never gates a match.

amenities.description: Optional amenity list for audit context. Informational; never gates a match.

GuestPromiseScore.description: Deterministic guest-promise score: if a guest booked the reference room, does the supplier room keep that promise? Computed from the physical attributes both names state (type, beds, capacity, view, balcony, access, tier, smoking, accessibility); meal plans, rate policies and marketing text are ignored. The audit model picks the reference; the score grades the pick and never raises it. Present on every mapped result, including exact matches and kept mappings (graded but never rewritten). Absent when the room was never mapped. The deductions are the system default or, for an account with its own scoring profile, that profile (see the scoring-profile endpoints).

score.description: 0 to 1. Starts at 1.0; each unconfirmed promise deducts its weight under the scoring profile in effect (default: view or bedrooms 0.30, balcony/terrace 0.25, lower tier 0.20, bed/tier/smoking 0.10, bed count/capacity/floor 0.05, inferred 0.05). 0 on a hard stop.

band.description: auto at or above the auto threshold (0.90 by default; a profile may raise it), review_sample >= 0.75 (use, sample), needs_review >= 0.60 (human look), not_mapped (hard stop or below 0.60).

hardStop.description: Reason code of the check that failed outright: structure_mismatch, bed_type_mismatch, no_confident_match, occupancy_mismatch, view_amenity_mismatch or restriction_mismatch.

core.description: Supplier name reduced to its physical room words (rate, meal and marketing text removed, common foreign room words translated).

flags.description: Non-scoring observations: single_use (sold for one guest), inconsistent_core (same physical room mapped to different references in this job), model_translated / reference_translated (graded on the model's English reading of a non-Latin supplier name / reference, returned in reading / referenceReading; same rules and weights as English), unreadable_name / unreadable_reference (non-Latin text with no reading: nothing to grade, so the mapping is held at review_sample), incomplete_catalog (some references of the hotel had no reading, so a hotel-wide inference could not be concluded; held at review_sample).

reading.description: The audit model's plain-English reading of a non-Latin supplier name, when the score was graded on it (flag model_translated).

referenceReading.description: The audit model's plain-English reading of a non-Latin reference room name, when the score was graded on it (flag reference_translated).

profile.description: The scoring policy the number was computed under: default, or your account's profile stamp such as c368927/v3 (see the scoring-profile endpoints).

reference.description: The reference room this score grades. Set even when the mapping was then rejected, so a rejection shows what the model picked.

decisive.description: True when this score decided the room's outcome (a mapping the model chose in this job: the score either rejected it or is final.confidence). Absent for an exact match, a kept mapping or a room the attribute guard rejected: those are graded for the breakdown only.

defaultScore.description: Only under an account profile: the same checks graded with the system default, so your number can always be compared with the neutral one.

defaultBand.description: Only under an account profile: the band of defaultScore.

attribute.description: structure, bedrooms, bed, bed_count, capacity, view, outdoor, access, tier, smoking, restriction, accessibility or location

promised.description: What the reference promises; empty when only the supplier states it

status.description: delivered: stated or a synonym. exceeded: supplier has more than promised (ignored). inferred: supplier silent but every reference of that type at the hotel has it. silent: not mentioned. conflict: supplier states the opposite.

delta.description: Amount deducted from 1.0 for this promise

knob.description: The scoring-profile weight that priced this deduction (view, bedrooms, outdoor, tier_lower, bed, tier, restriction, minor, inferred). Absent when nothing was deducted.

code.description: On a conflict: the reason code it stops with (or would stop with, when the profile softened it).

fail.description: On a conflict a profile may soften: access, outdoor_negated, bed_count or bedrooms.

value.description: Deduction in effect under this profile

description.example: Reference promises a view the supplier room does not mention

softened.description: True when this profile turns the fail into a deduction instead of rejecting the mapping

deduction.description: What a softened fail costs under this profile (never less than the matching silent weight)

description.example: Reference promises spa / club / pool / beach access the supplier room never mentions
Wrong room type in either direction (Room, Suite, Studio, Apartment, Villa)

adjustable.description: Only auto is adjustable, and only upwards

description.example: Lowest score that is still auto. May be raised, never lowered

ScoringProfile.description: Your account's scoring profile as it applies: every weight with its value, default and allowed range; the four fails you may soften; the rules nobody can change; the band thresholds. Rendered from the same catalogue the validator enforces, so what is marked adjustable is exactly what a PUT accepts.

name.description: default, or your tenant stamp (c<accountId> live, s<accountId> sandbox). With version it is the score.profile stamp on results.

version.description: Increments on every PUT and is never reused, even after a DELETE; 0 for the default.

isDefault.description: True when the account has no profile and the system default applies

updatedBy.description: The account id that made the change

ScoringProfileRequest.description: A full replacement of the profile. Every field is optional; a weight left out takes its default, an empty softened list softens nothing, an omitted autoThreshold is 0.90. Unknown fields are rejected (400), so a typo cannot silently reset a knob.

weights.description: Deduction per knob key (view, bedrooms, outdoor, tier_lower, bed, tier, restriction, minor, inferred), each within the range GET reports.

softened.description: Fails that become a deduction instead of rejecting the mapping

autoThreshold.description: Lowest score that is still auto; 0.90 to 1.00

ScoringPreviewRequest.description: When profile is omitted, the job is re-graded under your current profile.

ScoringPreview.description: What a candidate profile would do to a completed job: arithmetic on the checks the job stored, no model call, nothing changed. Only rooms whose outcome the score decided are counted; exact matches, kept mappings and guard rejections are reported as notDecidedByScore because no profile moves them.

scoredUnder.description: The profile stamps the stored results carry

candidate.description: candidate when a profile was sent, default when your account has none

graded.description: Rooms whose outcome the score decided

changed.description: Graded rooms whose score or band would move

after.description: Graded rooms per band under the candidate

changes.description: Up to 200 rooms that would move

afterHardStop.description: Set when the candidate would reject the room outright

truncated.description: True when more than 200 rooms would move

hotels.description: Hotels whose stored mappings were removed

skippedBusy.description: All-hotels purge only: hotels left untouched because a job was in flight

busyHotels.description: All-hotels purge only: up to 100 of the skipped hotels

get.summary: List partners available for hotel ID mapping
get.description:
## Overview

Returns every partner that can be used for hotel ID mapping, along with each partner's inventory coverage size (`mappings`). Use this list to discover which partner inventories can be aligned with Nuitee / liteAPI hotel IDs.

Hotel mapping connects a partner's hotel identifiers to Nuitee catalogue IDs so you can shop, book, and enrich content against a single inventory.

## When to Use

- **Before mapping IDs** - Confirm the partner name to pass into `POST /hotels/match/partners/with-id`
- **Coverage checks** - Compare `mappings` counts to estimate how much of a partner's inventory is already linked
- **Partner selectors** - Populate UI or automation dropdowns with supported partners
- **Onboarding** - Discover which OTAs / suppliers are available for ID-to-ID mapping

## What You Get

- **Partner names** - Exact strings to send as the `partner` form field on the map endpoint
- **Inventory size** - `mappings` count per partner (known ID links in the mapping catalogue)
- **Sorted list** - Partners ordered by mapping count, descending

## Key Features

- **No request body**: Simple authenticated GET
- **Case-insensitive partner names upstream**: Prefer the exact `partner` string from this response
- **Accounts without suppliers**: Allowed to call hotel mapping endpoints (standard auth still applies)

## Quick Start

1. Authenticate with your LiteAPI `X-API-Key`
2. Call `GET /hotels/match/partners`
3. Pick a `partner` value from the response
4. Upload that partner's hotel ID CSV to `POST /hotels/match/partners/with-id`

**Rate limit:** 50 requests/min (production), 10 requests/min (sandbox).

200.description: Partner list with inventory mapping counts

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid API key

post.summary: Map partner hotel IDs to Nuitee inventory
post.description:
## Overview

Maps a specific partner's hotel inventory to Nuitee / liteAPI catalogue IDs. Upload a CSV of partner hotel IDs and receive a result CSV that links each row to Nuitee property identifiers.

This is the synchronous **partner ID → Nuitee ID** mapping path. Processing runs in one request: CSV in, mapped CSV out (plus an `X-Mapping-Summary` header with outcome counts).

## When to Use

- **Partner inventory alignment** - Convert Booking.com, Expedia, or other partner hotel IDs into Nuitee `core_property_id` / `lite_property_id`
- **Bulk ID resolution** - Map large partner ID lists in a single call
- **Coverage analysis** - Use `matched`, `review`, `not_found`, and `invalid` counts from `X-Mapping-Summary`
- **Content & rates pipelines** - Resolve partner IDs before search, booking, or enrichment against Nuitee inventory

## What You Get

- **Result CSV** - Per-row mapping outcomes with columns such as `input_id`, `status`, `resolution`, `core_property_id`, `lite_property_id`, `candidate_core_ids`
- **Summary header** - `X-Mapping-Summary` JSON with `rows`, `matched`, `review`, `not_found`, `invalid`
- **Download filename** - `Content-Disposition` attachment name from the server (for example `id-mapping-Expedia.csv`)

## Key Features

- **Partner-scoped**: Mapping runs against one partner inventory at a time (`partner` form field)
- **Flexible CSV input**: Single ID column (with or without header), or multi-column files with a recognized ID header
- **Optional geo columns**: Latitude/longitude improve resolution when partner IDs are ambiguous
- **Streamed response**: Result CSV is streamed; there is no `{"data": ...}` JSON wrapper

## Quick Start

1. Call `GET /hotels/match/partners` and copy the partner name
2. Prepare a CSV of that partner's hotel IDs
3. `POST` `multipart/form-data` with:
   - `partner` — partner name from step 1
   - `file` — the CSV
4. Save the response body as CSV and read `X-Mapping-Summary` for counts

**Accepted ID column names** (case-insensitive): `id`, `hotel_id`, `hotelid`, `hotel_code`, `provider_id`, `provider_hotel_id`, `provider_property_id`, `partner_id`, `partner_hotel_id`, `property_id`, `code`.

**Example curl:**

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url "https://api.liteapi.travel/v3.0/hotels/match/partners/with-id" \
  --header "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  --form "partner=Booking.com" \
  --form "file=@/path/to/partner-ids.csv;type=text/csv"
```

Authenticate with your LiteAPI `X-API-Key`.

**Rate limit:** 50 requests/min (production), 10 requests/min (sandbox).

**Platform note:** Cloud Run and the global load balancer cap request/response bodies at 32 MiB. Larger uploads may not fully pass through this API hop.

partner.description: Partner name from GET /hotels/match/partners. Selects which partner inventory to map against Nuitee.

file.description: CSV of partner hotel IDs to map to Nuitee inventory

200.description: Result CSV mapping partner IDs to Nuitee inventory

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename for the result CSV

400.description: Bad Request — missing partner, unknown partner, or unreadable CSV

value.error: could not find an id column; …

401.description: Unauthorized — missing or invalid API key

post.summary: Submit an async hotel-match batch job
post.description:
## Overview

Upload an onboarding CSV of hotel rows (name, country, optional address/coordinates) and start an async **content-based** hotel matching job. Returns immediately with a `job_id` to poll.

Use this when partner hotel IDs are unavailable and you need to match hotels by content against Nuitee inventory.

## When to Use

- **Bulk onboarding** - Match many hotels by name/location when partner IDs are not available
- **Large files** - Jobs above the inline row limit are processed via chunked workers
- **GCS workflows** - Submit with `input_gcs` / `output_gcs` for large files outside the API body limit

## What You Get

- **202 Accepted** - Initial `JobStatus` with `status: queued` and `job_id`
- **Progress polling** - Use `GET /hotels/match/async/jobs/{jobId}/status` until `status` is `done` or `error`
- **Result CSV** - Download via `GET /hotels/match/async/jobs/{jobId}` when complete

## Quick Start

1. POST `multipart/form-data` with `file` (CSV), or JSON `{ "input_gcs": "gs://..." }` for large files
2. Poll status with the returned `job_id`
3. Download the result CSV when `status` is `done`

Input CSV must include `name` and `country` columns (accepted header aliases vary upstream). Optional `output_gcs` writes the result directly to GCS instead of returning CSV through the API.

Authenticate with your LiteAPI `X-API-Key`.

**Rate limit:** 50 requests/min (production), 10 requests/min (sandbox).

**Platform note:** Multipart uploads are capped at 32 MiB through this API hop — use GCS input mode for larger files.

output_gcs.description: Optional GCS URI for the result CSV

example.error: CSV exceeds 32MiB; use input_gcs for large files

get.description:
## Overview

Returns the current progress and verdict counts for an async hotel-match job.

## When to Use

- **Poll after submit** - Call repeatedly until `status` is `done` or `error`

## What You Get

- **Job counters** - `total`, `done`, `matched`, `review`, `no_match`, and conflict-class counts
- **Terminal states** - `done` means the result is ready (unless `output_gcs` was set); `error` includes an `error` message

## Quick Start

Use the `job_id` from the submit response.

**Rate limit:** 50 requests/min (production), 10 requests/min (sandbox).

## Overview

Streams the finished result CSV for a completed async hotel-match job.

## When to Use

- **After job completes** - Call when status polling returns `status: done` and no `output_gcs` was requested at submit time

## What You Get

- **Result CSV** - One row per input hotel with verdict, matched IDs, scores, and reasons
- **Attachment header** - `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="hotel-match-{jobId}.csv"`

## Quick Start

Poll until `status` is `done`, then download this endpoint. If submit included `output_gcs`, read that URI instead — this endpoint returns **409**.

**Rate limit:** 50 requests/min (production), 10 requests/min (sandbox).

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename for the result CSV

404.description: Unknown job or result not ready

value.error: result not available (job still running or expired)

post.summary: Match supplier rooms to a reference catalog
post.description:
**What it does:** For each supplier room, returns the best **reference room** match with confidence scores and ranked alternatives.

**Workflow role:** Optional **step 0** — quick sync scoring before async hotel jobs.

**Use when:** You need an **immediate** answer with `suppliers`. Either send `references` yourself, **or** omit `references` and set **`hotelId`** so the service resolves the catalog (`room_mapping_catalog` → LiteAPI data API; your references win if supplied; max 500 rooms).

**Do not use when:** You need persisted mappings, audit reasons, or room attributes — use `POST /rooms/match/async`. Not for clustering without a catalog — use `POST /rooms/group`.

**If `references` is omitted:** missing `hotelId` or unresolvable catalog → **400**; Redis or data API failure → **500**; suppliers×references over upstream cap → **413** when configured.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

hotelId.description: Hotel ID used to resolve the reference catalog when `references` is omitted. Required in that case; echoed in the response.

threshold.description: Minimum confidence score for a positive match

topK.description: Number of ranked candidates returned per supplier

references.description: Optional. Allowed mapping targets (the catalog). Omit or send empty to resolve the hotel catalog from `room_mapping_catalog:{hotelId}` (dispatcher-owned, read-only here), then the LiteAPI data API. Caller-supplied rooms win. Resolved catalogs are capped upstream (default 500) and never truncated; `hotelId` is required when this is omitted.

post.summary: Submit an async room mapping job
post.description:
**What it does:** Starts a **background mapping job** for one hotel (`jobId` to poll).

**Workflow role:** **Step 1** — create or refresh hotel mappings.

**Use when:** Hotel onboarding, catalog refresh, or sending trusted **attributes** (`supplierRooms`, optional `referenceRooms`, `attributeDetail`).

**Do not use when:** You only need instant sync scores — use `POST /rooms/match`.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

referenceRooms.description: Optional. Allowed mapping targets (the catalog). Omit or send empty to score against our hotel catalog, which the service resolves automatically. When supplied, the caller's list wins. Rejected above 500 rooms; the same limit applies to the catalog resolved on your behalf. Attributes are optional per room.

supplierRooms.description: Supplier rooms to map. Blank names are dropped and normalized duplicates removed; max 100 after deduplication. Name-only objects are valid. Every job is audited with attributes on both sides: our catalog attributes are added to the references, and facets stated in room names are derived on both sides.

provider.description: Source supplier for this room (for example `expedia`, `booking.com`, `agoda`, or any raw provider token). Overrides the job-level `provider` for this room. Copied to the room's `final.p` field. Providers are stored as a sorted, deduplicated, `|`-joined set, so a `|` is rejected here.

Source supplier of the submitted room names (for example `expedia`, `booking.com`, `hotelbeds`). Copied to every decision's `final.p` field, echoed on the job and on the `202` response, and persisted only when the job writes an isolated customer cache. `supplierRooms[].provider` overrides it per room. When the mapping already carries a provider, the supplied one is merged into that set. Must not contain `|`. Leave unset to keep the previous behaviour.

attributeDetail.description: How much attribute context the audit receives. `none` sends names only; `summary` (default) sends structure, tier, bedrooms, beds, bedRelation, occupancy, size, views and accessibility; `full` adds features and amenities. Applies to both supplier and reference attributes. The full request is always stored on the job.

provider.description: Source supplier echoed from the request, for the rooms that were submitted. Omitted when the request did not set one or when rooms carry different providers.

400.description: Bad Request - malformed JSON or validation failure. Also returned when `hotelId` is missing, when `supplierRooms` is missing or empty, when `referenceRooms` is omitted and no catalog can be resolved for the hotel, when a room attribute is unusable (negative counts, non-positive sizes, a size without a unit, an empty `beds[].type`, duplicate feature keys, or attributes over the size caps), when attributes exceed 4 KiB per room or 256 KiB per list, when `attributeDetail` is unknown, when `provider` is over 128 characters or contains `|`, or when the supplied or automatically resolved catalog exceeds 500 rooms. Unfamiliar attribute values are accepted.

value.error: deep-map validation error: hotelId is required
deep-map validation error: referenceRooms was not provided and the hotel catalog could not be resolved; provide referenceRooms or retry later
deep-map validation error: supplierRooms[0].attributes.beds[0].type must not be empty
deep-map validation error: fetched catalog exceeds max of 500

409.description: Conflict - a deep-map job is already in flight for this hotel

example.error: deep-map job already in flight for hotel: dm_1777386480123456789_a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8

500.description: Internal Server Error. Also returned as `failed to resolve reference rooms` when `referenceRooms` was omitted and the hotel data API could not be reached.

get.summary: Get async room mapping job status
get.description:
**What it does:** Job **status** and per-room **`confirm` / `remap` / reject** with `reasonCode`.

**Workflow role:** **Step 2** — poll every 5–10 s after async submit.

**Use when:** You have a `jobId`.

**Do not use when:** You only need the saved dictionary — use `GET /rooms/match/async/matches/{hotelId}`.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

currentMappingCount.description: Number of mappings available before this job ran.

provider.description: Source supplier supplied with the job, when one was set. Per-room values live on `supplierRooms[].provider`.

supplierRooms.description: Supplier rooms as stored on the job, including attributes when they were supplied.

provider.description: Source supplier recorded for this room, if any.

attributeDetail.description: Detail level used for the audit. Defaults to summary.

get.summary: Get saved room mappings for a hotel
get.description:
**What it does:** **Saved mapping dictionary** for your account and hotel.

**Workflow role:** **Step 3** — runtime lookup after mappings exist.

**Use when:** Resolving supplier names in search or book.

**Do not use when:** You need audit detail — use the job endpoint.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

delete.summary: Purge your saved room mappings for a hotel
delete.description:
**What it does:** Deletes every saved mapping of **your account** for the hotel, so the next `POST /rooms/match/async` for it grades every room afresh, for example under a new scoring profile. Nothing else is touched. `409` while a job of yours is in flight for the hotel.

Destructive and immediate; every purge is written to your mapping audit log.

Available to accounts with their own isolated room-mapping cache; others receive `409`. Details: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

409.description: A job is in flight for this hotel, or your account has no isolated cache

example.error: hotel has a deep-map job in flight

delete.summary: Purge all your saved room mappings
delete.description:
**What it does:** Deletes every saved mapping of **your account**, across all hotels. Requires `?confirm=<your account id>`; the dispatcher checks it before forwarding and the mapping service checks it again. A hotel with a job of yours in flight is skipped, not purged, and listed in `busyHotels`. One run per minute (`429`).

Destructive and immediate; every purge is written to your mapping audit log.

Available to accounts with their own isolated room-mapping cache; others receive `409`. Details: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

parameters.name: confirm
parameters.description: Must equal your LiteAPI account id

example.error: confirm must equal your account id

409.description: Your account does not have an isolated room-mapping cache; scoring profiles and purges need one (contact LiteAPI to enable it)

example.error: scoring profiles require an isolated customer cache (X-Customer-Cache: customer)

429.description: An all-hotels purge ran less than a minute ago

example.error: an all-hotels purge ran less than a minute ago

get.description:
**What it does:** Returns the scoring policy your room matches are graded with: every weight with its current value, default and allowed range, the four fails you may soften, the rules nobody can change, and the band thresholds. `isDefault: true` when you have not set one.

**Use when:** Rendering a settings page, or checking which policy a `score.profile` stamp refers to.

Available to accounts with their own isolated room-mapping cache; others receive `409`. Details: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

weights.description: Reference promises a view the supplier room does not mention

softenableFails.description: Reference promises spa / club / pool / beach access the supplier room never mentions

fixedRules.description: Wrong room type in either direction (Room, Suite, Studio, Apartment, Villa)

thresholds.description: Lowest score that is still auto. May be raised, never lowered

409.description: Your account does not have an isolated room-mapping cache; scoring profiles and purges need one (contact LiteAPI to enable it)

example.error: scoring profiles require an isolated customer cache (X-Customer-Cache: customer)

put.description:
**What it does:** Replaces your scoring profile. The body is validated against the ranges `GET` reports before anything is stored; an out-of-range weight, an unknown knob, a fail that cannot be softened or an `autoThreshold` below 0.90 is refused with `400` and the message names the field. Unknown fields are `400` too.

**Takes effect on new jobs only.** Mappings already stored keep the score they were stored with. To re-score a hotel, purge its matches (`DELETE /rooms/match/async/matches/{hotelId}`) and submit it again. Preview a candidate first with `POST /rooms/match/async/scoring-profile/preview`.

Each change gets a new `version` that is never reused; `score.profile` on results (for example `c368927/v3`) names the exact policy that produced the number.

Available to accounts with their own isolated room-mapping cache; others receive `409`. Details: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

weights.description: Reference promises a view the supplier room does not mention

softenableFails.description: Reference promises spa / club / pool / beach access the supplier room never mentions

**What it does:** Removes your profile; new jobs are graded with the system default again. The version counter is kept, so a profile set later never reuses an old stamp. Stored mappings are not touched.

Available to accounts with their own isolated room-mapping cache; others receive `409`. Details: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

post.summary: Preview a scoring profile on a completed job
post.description:
**What it does:** Re-grades a completed job of yours under a candidate profile (or your current one when `profile` is omitted) and reports every room whose score or band would move. It is arithmetic on the checks the job stored: no model call, nothing is changed, and it does not show what the model would have picked differently.

Only rooms whose outcome the score decided are counted (`graded`); exact matches, kept mappings and guard rejections are reported as `notDecidedByScore` since no profile moves them. A job that is not completed, or one scored before profiles existed, is `400`.

Available to accounts with their own isolated room-mapping cache; others receive `409`. Details: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

post.summary: Group rooms without a reference catalog
post.description:
**What it does:** Clusters supplier room names **without** a reference catalog.

**Workflow role:** Outside the main four-step flow — exploration only.

**Use when:** You do not have catalog rooms yet.

**Do not use when:** You have a catalog — use `/rooms/match` or async.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).

**What it does:** Assigns each supplier room to **one reference bucket**.

**Workflow role:** Alternate **sync** view (not step 0 of the main flow).

**Use when:** You want reference-centric grouping instead of per-supplier scores.

**Do not use when:** You need ranked candidates or async persistence.

Details, examples, limits, and result codes: **Implementation Workflow** (doc page: `implementation-workflow`).
